about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.agency: U.S. Geological Survey and Chattahoochee Riverkeeper (BacteriALERT)
channels.name: Chattahoochee River BacteriALERT
channels.note: Chattahoochee River BacteriALERT: weekly E. coli samples (reported within 24 hours) and turbidity-based E. coli estimates at three USGS stations in the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, a program with Chattahoochee Riverkeeper. Voluntary monitoring; results, not overflow notices. Answered 200 to the project user agent on 2026-11-04 (the page then said the estimate could not be calculated because of gage maintenance). Chattahoochee Riverkeeper's own BacteriALERT addresses answered 301 that day (to an image and to a blog post on the program's 20 years). The page offers a weekly e-mail of the sampled counts. (research/ga/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (ECHO)
channels.note: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event records (NPDES eReporting). Voluntary publication by EPA: Georgia permittees file 24-hour and 5-day reports in EPD's GEOS and these reach EPA (times and end, no volume). Covers every operator in the state. (research/ga/report.md §2.2)

channels.name: Georgia Environmental Protection Division
channels.note: EPD's Municipal Sewage Spills Reported to EPD: a rolling 30-day workbook posted each business day at a dated URL (begin day, permit, address, gallons, waterway). Voluntary publication: the rule requires the operator to tell EPD, not EPD to post. Does not say whether the public was notified. Covers every operator in the state. (research/ga/report.md §2.2)
